name: answer_notification
description:
Settle one entry from `list_notifications`, whichever kind it is.

A question takes `answer` and `basis`. A permission — a `tap_out`, or an
agent asking to call something — takes `decision`: `allow` or `deny`.

`basis` says what an answer rests on and is checked: `record` means the
project records it, `precedent` means the user already decided it and takes
`precedent_id`, `inspected` means you read it yourself and takes `citation`
— a file path, commit, or tool call you actually made in this session, close
enough to your own wording that it is checkable there. An answer with none
of these is a guess and is refused — say what you found it in, or escalate.

Say `worked_around` when you had to supply something the asking role should
have been able to find itself; that gets counted as a gap in that role's
tools. Say `capability` alongside it: a short, stable name for what was
missing (usually the tool name), not a sentence. `worked_around` is written
fresh each time and rarely matches word for word between occurrences of the
same gap, so without `capability` the same gap can get filed as several
issues instead of one counted repeatedly.

answer.description: What you found, in the agent's terms. For a question, the answer. For a denied tap_out, why it was denied — the agent is told this, and without it all it hears is 'declined', so it re-reads its own transcript and repeats whatever it last concluded.

basis.description: For a question: `record` (the project records it), `precedent`, or `inspected`.

capability.description: With `worked_around`: a short, stable name for what was missing — the tool name, normalized, not a sentence. Lets the same gap, described differently each time, still count as one.

citation.description: With basis `inspected`: the file path, commit, or tool call you actually made in this session — checked against your own turns, so it has to be close to how you actually wrote or called it, not a paraphrase.

on_behalf_of.description: A role you are acting as. Usually leave this out.

precedent_id.description: With basis `precedent`: the question they answered.

tool.description: A tool you are using on that role's behalf.

worked_around.description: The capability the asking role lacked, if you covered for one.

name: cadence
description:
How often you are woken to look in on your agents, and whether you are being
woken at all.

Called with no arguments it reports; `seconds` sets the interval and `woken`
turns the waking on or off. Twenty minutes is the starting default and it was a guess — it is
the one number trading the feature's two costs against each other, and the
right value is not knowable in advance. Too long and a stalled agent burns
most of a window before anybody looks; too short and the check-ins cost more
than they find on a machine that is also running the agents.

Reports two separate things, because they are separate and conflating them is
how a broken cadence stayed invisible:

  * **woken** — whether this project is meant to be woken at all, or has stood
    down. A decision, and it survives a restart.
  * **running** — whether a timer actually exists right now. A fact.

They disagree in exactly the case worth catching: meant to be woken, and
nothing there to wake it.

seconds.description: Set the interval to this many seconds. Omit to report without changing it.

woken.description: false stands this project down so nothing wakes it; true resumes. Omit to leave it alone.

name: check_in
description:
Look in on your agents now, without waiting for the next scheduled wake-up.

The same digest the cadence delivers — what every agent is working on, the
health of the machinery under them, and every question waiting on somebody.
Assembled from all three, so a failure in any one of them is reported as a
failure rather than as a shorter list: an empty digest and an unbuildable one
read identically, and only one of them is good news.

The cadence is a floor, never a schedule — the longest anything can go unseen.
Nothing here waits for it: a question raised now is pushed now, and this is
how you look when you have a reason to rather than when the timer says so.

name: check_machinery
description:
Whether the things your agents depend on are working: the harness, the tool
surface, the preview, the analyzers and the machine itself.

Ask it when an agent misbehaves, before restarting anything. A fault every
agent shares is one fault underneath them and restarting them will not reach
it; a fault one agent has while its neighbours work is that agent's.

Healthy is reported as well as broken, so you can rule the machinery out.

name: completion_handoff
description: Assign reviewed artifact preservation, inspect completions, and explicitly acknowledge their next action. No action certifies QA or starts promotion.

name: escalate_question
description:
Hand one of your agents' questions to the user, with why you could not answer.

Use it when the decision is theirs — what to build, what it is worth, which
way the product goes. Not for anything the project already records: look that
up and answer it.

The question stays open and stays in your listing, marked as waiting on them.

as.description: The same question as a choice about their product. Put it in their words when the agent's were module names — the original travels with it.

reason.description: Why this is the user's call and not yours. They read it.

to.description: `user` (the default) to escalate; `main` or `product` to hand it to the other answerer instead, without the user seeing it.

name: list_agent_work
description:
What every agent on this project is doing, across all its working copies.

For each: the task it holds and the story behind it, when it last said
anything, whether a turn is still running, what it is waiting on, and what is
wrong on its checkout.

Facts, not a verdict — whether an agent is stuck is your call to make from
them.

name: list_notifications
description:
Everything the agents on this project are waiting on, in one place.

Questions and permissions together — a `tap_out` stops an agent exactly as an
unanswered question does. Grouped by who holds each one: yours to answer, or
already sent up and waiting on the user. `kind` says whether it takes an
answer or a decision. Settle any of them with `answer_notification`.

name: list_offers
description:
Every nudge the harness sent this project's agents, as offers with outcomes.

A kind × status count table, then the newest offers (default 50) with their
subject, attempt, status and the messages they were sent as. `undelivered`
never reached the agent. Filters: `agent_id`, `kind`, `status`, `since`
(ISO8601), `limit`.

kind.description: work, menu, problems, resume, retry, answer, unblocked, check_in or stalled.

limit.description: How many offers to show, newest first. Defaults to 50.

since.description: ISO8601 — only offers made at or after this time.

status.description: open, claimed, declined, ignored, superseded, expired, n_a or undelivered.

name: read_agent_conversation
description:
Read what one or more of your agents has said, most recent turns last.

For finding out what a stuck agent was doing without spending its turn on
the question. `agent_id` reads one agent; `agent_ids` merges several onto
one timeline. `limit` bounds how many turns come back; a read that would
be too large is cut to the recent end and says so. `since`/`until` (ISO8601)
narrow to a window. `last_call_of` skips the transcript and answers only
the last call to that tool and what it returned.

agent_id.description: From `list_agent_work`, or its conversation id. One of this or `agent_ids`.

agent_ids.description: Several agents, merged onto one timeline.

last_call_of.description: Skip the transcript — answer only the last call to this tool and its result.

limit.description: Most recent N turns. Defaults to a page.

since.description: ISO8601 — only turns at or after this time.

until.description: ISO8601 — only turns at or before this time.

name: ready_stories_without_epic
description:
Ready stories that belong to no epic.

The reading that lets you answer "which ready story is outside every epic" —
which nothing else exposes. `list_epics` lists epics and `assign_story_to_epic`
writes one; neither says which stories are in none of them.

name: reset_doc_packages
description:
Puts failed hex doc packages back in the queue: `failed` markers become
`pending` with no attempts, and the next sweep tries them again. For
failures whose cause has been fixed. Narrow with `packages`, `except` or
`error_like`; with none, every failed package is reset. Returns the count.

error_like.description: Only failures whose error contains this text, e.g. unique_violation.

name: restart_agent
description:
Restart one of your agents, saying why.

The reason is not a label: it is checked against what has already been tried.
A restart for a reason that has been tried and did not work is refused and
raised as an issue instead, because restarting something restarting does not
fix is a loop with a cost.

Restarts one agent. Not the harness — that would kill in-flight work on every
checkout on the machine, other projects included.

reason.description: What you are restarting it to fix. Checked against what was already tried.

name: resume_issue_qa
description: Authorize audited QA resumption after an operational partial. Preserves historical attempts; does not certify QA or launch execution.

attempt_id.description: Latest immutable partial QA attempt being resumed

candidate_sha.description: Full preserved candidate SHA independently verified by main

operational_only.description: Explicit main attestation of operational interruption rather than implementation failure

reason.description: Operational prerequisite and evidence that it is now cleared

name: search_answers
description:
Decisions the user has already made, matching some words.

Look here before escalating. A question they have answered before does not
need asking again — pass the id to `answer_question` as `precedent_id` with
basis `precedent`.

Answered questions only. An open one matching the same words is the opposite
of a precedent: evidence that this has been asked and not decided.

query.description: Words from the question you are handling.

name: set_agent_continuous
description:
Put one of your agents in the loop, or let it leave.

Starting an agent and putting it to work are different acts, and only the
first had a tool. An agent that is started but not continuous takes one turn
and stops, so a fleet could be started and still do nothing — which is what
"my agents are not running" turns out to mean most times it is said.

Answers what actually happened, because switching on is not one outcome. The
flag alone marks an agent willing and leaves it where it was: an agent is a
supervised process that acts when messaged, and nothing polls. So this rings
its bell too, and says whether the bell reached something.

continuous.description: True puts it in the loop and wakes it. False lets it stop after its current turn.

name: take_over_work
description:
Ask to take a task off an agent. **This always refuses.**

It exists to say no, and the no is the feature. Your wider scope is for what a
role cannot do, not for what you would rather not wait for — including when an
agent is being slow. Each individual takeover is defensible; the end state is
one agent doing everything with three idle, decided by nobody.

Where you legitimately act past a role's reach, act directly rather than
confiscating its task — `ready_stories_without_epic` is the worked example, and
that already works.

Said plainly here because the refusal reads like an assessment of the task and
is not one: `task_id` is accepted and never consulted, so the answer is the
same whatever you pass. Nothing specifies when a takeover should succeed, so
nothing does.

task_id.description: The task you want to take on.

name: validation_hold
description: Record, authorize and hand off serial validation. Listing includes terminal and unknown execution evidence; no action launches a run.

action.description: list, create, authorize, release or confirm_termination

run_id.description: On create, adopt this project's existing active run rather than start another.

termination_evidence.description: Verified terminal evidence for confirm_termination; never a guess or timeout alone.
